notable_absence.finding: None to report - this is the third page in the batch to demonstrate results.close() actually being called (`results.close();` on the line immediately after the for-loop), and arguably the most important one to get right: it is a self-recursive, potentially many-invocation handler, exactly the case where a leaked cursor would compound across reinvocations rather than staying a one-off. It closes correctly.

cross_component_finding: Confirms the twin's own point unchanged: self_recursion is passed as the 4th argument to couchbase.upsert (`couchbase.upsert(src_col, meta, doc, { "self_recursion": true });`), an Advanced Keyspace Accessor call taking the src_col bucket-alias binding explicitly - the self_recursion mechanism is a KV/upsert-option concern layered on top of the Advanced Keyspace Accessor family, not a N1QL-specific one, even though the workload it happens to paginate here is inline SQL++.
